item.research_question: How can the thermodynamic formation barrier of high-valence metal species be minimized to enable the lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LOM) for enhanced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity in multicomponent alloys?
item.material_system: Multicomponent FeCoCrNi alloy film (nominally equiatomic) and its surface-reconstructed (oxy)hydroxide (FeCoCrNi OER catalyst); compared with FeCrNi and CoCrNi alloys
item.processing_route: Magnetron sputtering to deposit ~100 nm MCA films on carbon cloth at room temperature (Ar flow 12 sccm, 10 rpm rotation); followed by electrochemical activation via 200 CV cycles (0–0.6 V vs Hg/HgO, 100 mV s⁻¹) in 1-M KOH to induce irreversible surface reconstruction into Cr-leached (oxy)hydroxides
item.test_conditions: OER activity measured in O₂-saturated 1-M KOH electrolyte at 25 °C; LSV sweep rate 5 mV s⁻¹ with 95%-iR compensation; stability tested via 3000 CV cycles (0.2–0.7 V vs Hg/HgO) and 20-h chronoamperometry at ~10 mA cm⁻²; ¹⁸O isotope-labeled experiments performed in sealed cell with N₂-saturated K¹⁶OH
key_findings: EA-FCCN delivers a mass activity of 3601 A gmetal⁻¹ and TOF of 0.483 s⁻¹ at 300 mV overpotential, significantly outperforming EA-FCN (1183 A gmetal⁻¹), EA-CCN (101 A gmetal⁻¹), and RuO₂ (37 A gmetal⁻¹).
The Tafel slope decreases from 51.4 mV dec⁻¹ (EA-CCN) to 38.7 mV dec⁻¹ (EA-FCCN), indicating accelerated reaction kinetics.

In situ Raman and ex situ sXAS confirm the dynamic formation of Ni⁴⁺ species in Fe-involved catalysts (EA-FCN and EA-FCCN) via a multistep evolution (Ni²⁺→Ni³⁺→Ni⁴⁺), whereas EA-CCN remains primarily Ni³⁺.
¹⁸O isotope-labeled experiments show that EA-FCCN and EA-FCN generate ¹⁶O¹⁸O and ¹⁸O₂ products, unambiguously proving lattice oxygen participation (LOM pathway), while EA-CCN does not.
Fe component induces electron depletion in Ni species via interatomic electronic interplay (Fe³⁺-O-Ni²⁺), lowering the energy barrier for Ni⁴⁺ formation.
The reconstructed catalyst exhibits excellent stability with only an 8 mV anodic shift after 3000 CV cycles and ~7% current decay after 20 h, unlike RuO₂ which deactivates within 6 h.
DFT simulations reveal that the LOM pathway on Fe-involved models has a lower energy barrier (1.43 eV for OH⁻ adsorption as RLS) compared to the AEM pathway (1.94 eV) and the CoCrNi model.
item.mechanism: The Fe component induces electron depletion in Ni species through interatomic electronic interplay (Fe³⁺-O-Ni²⁺), facilitating a multistep evolution of Ni²⁺→Ni³⁺→Ni⁴⁺. The dynamically formed Ni⁴⁺ species drives holes into oxygen ligands, making them electrophilic and triggering intramolecular oxygen coupling (LOC) via a Mars-van Krevelen-like mechanism. This lattice oxygen activation (LOM) pathway leads to the formation of an Fe–Ni dual-site with oxygen vacancies as the ultimate catalytic center, substantially lowering the limiting energy barrier for OER.
item.limitations: The authors state that intrinsic activity values are inevitably underestimated because only surface metal species provide active sites, not the whole deposited alloy film. They also note that the Pourbaix diagrams indicate deep oxidation of metal species usually requires elevated potentials, making highly oxidized species thermodynamically unfavorable without specific engineering.
item.future_work: The authors propose that this work endows a guideline for the exploration of advanced OER electrocatalysts and broadens the applications of multicomponent alloy materials toward catalysis, implying future designs should focus on engineering interatomic electronic interplay to stabilize high-valence species.
quotes: Fe component enables the formation of Ni4+ species, which is energetically favored by the multistep evolution of Ni2+→Ni3+→Ni4+.
The dynamically constructed Ni4+ species drives holes into oxygen ligands to facilitate intramolecular oxygen coupling, triggering lattice oxygen activation.
EA-FCCN delivers a high mass activity of 3601 A gmetal−1 at an overpotential of 300 mV, while 1183, 101, and 37 A gmetal−1 are only observed for EA-FCN, EA-CCN, and RuO2, respectively.
